records.name: Missouri
records.summary: Bans gender-affirming medical care for minors (the SAFE Act, in force since 28 August 2023 after a judge declined to block it) and restricts access to such treatment for people in prisons, jails and correctional centres, with providers facing licence revocation; no adult facility ban recorded. Slightly below the national score 0.36.

records.name: Alaska
records.summary: Moderate tier in the July 2026 legal-risk assessment (grouped with Kentucky and North Carolina): one or two laws aimed at transgender adults or several aimed at youth, but no adult facility ban recorded and no protective statute. Slightly below the national score 0.36.

records.name: Georgia
records.summary:
A July 2026 data analysis places Georgia's recorded killing rate for trans women at 4.8 per 100k per year — among the country's highest — and a Georgia law-review article documents the long-run fatality concentration around Atlanta: at least 15 fatal cases statewide across 1990–2014 (11 in Atlanta) and 16 more across 2015–2023 (8 in Atlanta). Both series are treated by their authors as undercount floors.

The same analysis's warning applies to Georgia directly: its legal-risk grade describes how the state behaves, not how its people do — here a jurisdiction whose documented danger to trans people has been violence on the street more than legislation from the legislature.

records.name: Pennsylvania
records.summary:
A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places Pennsylvania in its 'low-risk states' group — largely refraining from targeting transgender adults while not specialising in protection.

A national equality tracker records no public-facility-use ban for Pennsylvania, leaving the state's profile for a trans visitor defined by that restraint rather than by any affirmative statute in either direction.

records.name: Wisconsin
records.summary:
An independent July 2026 assessment of anti-trans legal risk across the United States classifies Wisconsin among the states that have "largely refrained from targeting transgender adults" while also not "taking extraordinary steps to protect" them — a comparatively low-risk state posture inside a federation whose overall rating for trans visitors fell after the 2025 federal rollbacks of identity documents and passport policy.

No Wisconsin-specific facility or care ban appears in the assessment's grading. The national equality-map project cataloguing state bathroom bans was cited by the research pass but its page could not be reloaded at fetch time, so it stands as a data source only.
